answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can post bids or claim rewards. When an independent, randomly selected quorum verifies a task, duplicate identities controlled by one actor cannot multiply valid claims; conflicting claims or provable fraud burn the deposit. The gale of cheap account creation then meets a harbor of bonded participation: each extra identity ties up real capital, while a successful attack risks losing it. A relic of trust is not enough; the attacker must fund every active identity and keep its stake exposed.
